sections.heading: DEFINITIONS
sections.text: For the purposes of this act- (a) The term “Law Enforcement Officer” means any individual being commissioned as an officer or agent of any federal law enforcement agency whose duty it is to carry out duties in enforcing the law. (b) The term "Lawful Order" means a directive or command issued by a duly authorized individual or entity, in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, or legal authority; compliance and adherence to a lawful order are mandated within the prescribed legal framework, without contravening statutory provisions, constitutional rights, or judicial precedents. (c) The term “Court” means the United States District Court for the District of Columbia, or in cases of appeals being taken, the Supreme Court of the United States. (d) The term “Felony” means a significant breach of the law, encompassing offenses of a grave nature; anything with a sentence longer than 8 days. (e) The term "Correctional Facility" means any penitentiary, prison or detainment facility within the District of Columbia.

sections.heading: ENFORCEMENT POWERS AND SENTENCING
sections.text: (1) Any Law Enforcement Officer shall be authorized to enforce the entirety of this Code and shall be empowered with the ability to make arrests without warrant for crimes committed in their presence. They shall require probable cause to make arrests, and/or reasonable suspicion to detain subjects, pursuant to the Constitution, and Law. (2) Sections 801 through to 805 in chapter 7 of this Code will only be enforceable by officers of the Metropolitan Police Department, and by any other such law enforcement officers as the Attorney General may designate. (3) When sentencing an individual the following should be taken into account: remorse, previous criminal behavior, attitude and cooperation with the Court, compliance with Orders. (4) All offenses established into this Code shall have a Class. (5) There shall be the following classes with the maximum sentence designations attached, for which the courts may order— (a) Class A - 20 days maximum; (b) Class B - 15 days maximum; (c) Class C - 12 days maximum; (d) Class D - 10 days maximum; (e) Class E - 8 days maximum; (f) Class F - 5 days maximum; (g) Class G - 3 days maximum. (6) There shall be the following initial in-game arrest with the maximum and minimum arrest time designations for each class attached– (a) Class A - 20 minutes maximum, 15 minutes minimum; (b) Class B - 15 minutes maximum, 10 minutes minimum; (c) Class C - 12 minutes maximum, 8 minutes minimum; (d) Class D - 10 minutes maximum, 6 minutes minimum; (e) Class E - 8 minutes maximum, 4 minutes minimum; (f) Class F - 5 minutes maximum, 3 minutes minimum; (g) Class G - 3 minutes minimum and maximum. (7) There shall be the following maximum citation designations for each class attached— (a) Class A -$50,000; (b) Class B - $40,000; (c) Class C - $30,000; (d) Class D - $25,000; (e) Class E - $15,000; (f) Class F - $10,000; (g) Class G - $5,000. (8) All sentences shall be served consecutively with 'Federal Prison' or whatever rank is adopted or remanded by Management in the future (9) All sentences handed down under this Code, should there be multiple, shall be handed down only to be served consecutively, never concurrently. (10) There shall be a statute of limitations for all offenses within this Code for seventy (70) days. (11) The Courts shall maintain the authority to establish their own sentencing guidelines, that shall not be inconsistent with the provisions of this act.

sections.heading: PROBATION AND PAROLE
sections.text: (1) There shall be options established for Judges to apply, when in writing: (a) Probation. The conditions of such probation may be set to be abided by the convicted and sentenced person concurrently with the service of their sentence and no longer thereafter. Such conditions shall not be unreasonable, unlawful or in conflict with common law, judicial decree or statutory law. (b) Parole. Conditions of such parole may be set to be abided by the convicted and sentenced person after serving their sentence for a period of no longer than fourteen days. Such conditions shall not be unreasonable, unlawful or in conflict with common law, judicial decree or statutory law. (2) The Department of Justice shall have the ability to record, follow and ordain the measures of Probation and Parole under the authority of the Attorney General.
